<!-- pr-reviewer: d92d8f1f13f807ec335b7d7f8811d74a83346812 -->
Safety review (Opus, read-only): clean

I read the diff, the full `assets/posts/wire-iso.cps` at `d92d8f1f1`, the emitters in `crates/app/src/posting_wire.rs` and the block in `crates/app/src/posting.rs:701-706`. I did not build. The author's gates and the heavy lanes for the cut gate are named in the PR body. The head merges cleanly with `origin/main` (`git merge-tree`).

Findings:

1. Refusal by name. `onParameter` (line 193) refuses `WireTaper`, `WirePlane`, `WireAngle`, `WireU` and `WireV` when `has(value)` is false. `has` is false for `null`, `undefined`, `"nan"`, `"inf"`, NaN and Infinity. The text names the param. The refusal is a `message()`, so `out.warnings` is not empty and `posting.rs:701` returns `post blocked`. No NC file is written.
2. No cut after the refusal. `cutOk` (line 335) returns false while `notFinite` is set. `onLinear` and `onCircular` both go through `cutOk`. Thus no G1, G2 or G3 of that section is written after the refusal, and the start hole and the thread words are not written either if the refusal comes first. `onSectionEnd` writes only the end words of a threaded wire. That output is in a blocked file.
3. Reset. `onSectionEnd` (line 454) sets `notFinite = ""`. A section-level param (`WireTaper`, `WirePlane`) comes before `onSection`, and `onSection` does not clear the flag. Thus a bad section taper blocks the cuts of its own section only. A later good section posts normally. The `refuse` key holds the op name, so a second op with the same fault also gives its own message.
4. Valid values. `has(0)` and `has(-0)` are true, and negative values are true. The old branches are not changed. No golden file changed. The inch path (`fu`) is not changed.
5. A param that is not stated. `onParameter` is not called for it, so the behaviour is the same as before. The app emitters always send an `f64` (`posting_wire.rs:220`, `234`, `322-323`, `402`; `Lean::Angle.plane` is `f64`). Thus a normal app stream never sends `null` for these params, and the new guard does not refuse a good program.
6. Test. `a_non_finite_wire_number_is_refused_by_name_and_writes_no_cut` has a good control section, then a bad `WireU` (`null`, `"nan"`, `"inf"`), a bad `WireV`, a bad `WireAngle` and a bad `WireTaper`. For each, it checks the refusal text and that the move is not written. The red proof on `a36ced552` agrees with the old script: a null `WireU` was skipped, and the move posted as a plain `G1` with no warning.
7. The decision file has the `## #3236 - ...` heading, Decided, Why, Dropped and Cost. It agrees with `docs/decisions/README.md`. The PR body has a `Changelog:` line and `Fixes #3236`. No process file changed. The provenance header of the script is kept.

Note, not a blocker: `has("")` and `has(true)` are true (JavaScript `isFinite`), so a hand-written `PARAM WireU` with an empty or boolean value reads as 0 or 1. This was so before this PR. The app never writes such a value. If someone wants it, a `P7` follow-up can check `typeof value`.

Heavy lanes: not run here. They go to the cut gate, as the PR body says. "Not run" is not a pass.

<!-- pr-reviewer: d92d8f1f13f807ec335b7d7f8811d74a83346812 -->
Second safety read (Opus, read-only): clean

Scope: I read `assets/posts/wire-iso.cps` at `d92d8f1f1` in full, the diff, `crates/post/src/post/cnc.rs` (`serialize`, `param_value`), the `Param` arm of `crates/post/src/post/engine.rs` and the `WireU` / `WireTaper` emitters in `crates/app/src/posting_wire.rs`. I did not build and did not run tests.

**How a bad number reaches the script**
- The app writes `json!(f64::NAN)` as JSON null. `serialize` writes `PARAM WireU null`.
- `param_value` parses only finite numbers to a JSON number. `null`, `nan`, `inf` and `1e400` come to the script as JS strings.
- `has("null")`, `has("nan")`, `has("inf")` and `has(NaN)` are all false (`isFinite` coerces the string to `NaN` or to `Infinity`). Thus the new guard at line 193 catches each of them.

**Hand traces**
- (a) A lean move with a null `WireU`: line 193 sets `notFinite = "WireU"` and refuses by name. `WireV 0` does not set `uv`, because `uv` is null. `onLinear` calls `cutOk`, and line 335 returns false. The script writes no G1. Before the fix, this move posted as a plain `G1 X Y`.
- (b) A null `WireAngle` on an angle-word machine: the same refusal by name. The move writes nothing, and no `ANaN` is possible.
- (c) A null `WireV`: the refusal names `WireV`. The old "states no taper" message at line 381 is not reached, because `cutOk` returns first.
- (d) A null `WireTaper`: the refusal names `WireTaper` before the section. `taper` stays 0. Each cut of the section stops at line 335, before `startCut`. Thus the script writes no G0, no thread and no G1.
- (e) A good section after a refused one: line 454 resets `notFinite` at `onSectionEnd`. The next section posts normally. The keys in `refused` stay, but they do not block a cut.
- (f) All values finite: `git diff origin/main d92d8f1f1 -- assets/posts/wire-iso.cps` is 14 added lines and no changed lines. When each value is finite, the guard at line 193 is false, line 335 is false, and line 454 resets an empty string. The output is byte-identical to main.
- A bad number in the middle of a section, after the thread: each later move and arc is refused. `onSectionEnd` writes `taper_off` and the wire cut. The NC file is blocked by the `message()` warning.

**No plain G1 and no NaN / Infinity**
- `onLinear` and `onCircular` both call `cutOk` first. While `notFinite` is set, no motion word is written.
- Each number that the script writes goes through `has()`: `fu` in `wo`, the U V template, the angle template, the plane note, the taper note, `orgX` / `orgY` and the arc I J. Thus no path writes `NaN` or `Infinity`.

**Non-blocking notes (follow-ups, not for this PR)**
1. `has()` is true for some values that are not numbers. These come only from a hand-written stream:
   - `PARAM WireU ""` gives `""`, and `Number("")` is 0, so the script writes `U0.`.
   - `PARAM WireU true` gives `true`, so the script writes `U1.`.
   - `PARAM WireU 0x1A` gives the string `"0x1A"`, so the script writes `U26.`.
   `param_value` already turns each finite number into a JSON number. Thus each string that comes to a wire number is bad. A guard of `typeof value !== "number" || !isFinite(value)` for `WIRE_NUMBERS` closes this gap. The app path is safe without it. I recommend a `P7` follow-up, or `P3` if you think that a hand-written stream is user input.
2. A null `WireTaper` on an angle-word machine also gives the message "an angle-word taper needs one stated angle" (line 248). The first message names the true cause, so this is only noise.
3. The test does not pin (e) (a good section after a refused one) or a bad `WirePlane`. I traced them by hand, and they are correct.
4. Out of scope: a non-finite `OriginX` / `OriginY` is still ignored without a word (lines 199-200). Then the offset stays 0 or keeps its old value. This is the same class of defect as #3236, so I recommend a separate issue.

Refusal messages: each one names the param and the cause, for example `operation Punch1: PARAM WireU is not a finite number (null) - refused, the wire post writes no cut from it`. None says "states no taper" for a bad number.

Coordinator: this PR fixes #3236, which is on the cut list of v0.25.0.

- Reviews this merge relies on, both clean, both on head d92d8f1f1: the Opus safety review (comment 7071252890) and the second Opus safety read (comment 7071263058).
- Gate on the exact head d92d8f1f1, by the author: a red proof on the old script (`script_wire_iso.rs:142`), then `script_wire_iso` 13 of 13; app `wire_post`, `wire_taper`, `wire_taper_angle`, `wire_4axis` and `conformance`, all pass; clippy `-p camcraft-post`, pass; `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`, 48 steps, 0 failed.
- Heavy lanes: not run here (7 app heavy lanes are reached). The maintainer decided that the heavy lanes of P1 floor PRs go to the cut gate.
- I flag it ready and merge it on head d92d8f1f1. Nothing is pushed after this flag.
